rv.q: A lesser-known selection from the composer and lyricist’s archive is full of heart and humour, swinging between cabaret blues and pop bangers.

It may not be revelatory, and occasionally it pushes too hard, but it is an often fascinating excavation of a gifted, influential artist's process that reminds us of what was and what might have been.
This important show demonstrates something of what the world lost when Jonathan Larson died in 1996 at the age of 35.
This is Larson’s budding, exploratory talent laid bare.
This production pays a fervent and authentic tribute to a man who was an advocate for living passionately and mindfully, choosing connection over fear.
Overall, The Jonathan Larson Project is a very enjoyable ninety minutes spent in talented company, showcasing many songs which are well worth hearing and which otherwise we would have missed.

The show which says and does exactly what it says on the tin and serves as a reminder of what we lost when 35 year old Larson, the composer of the dazzling musical RENT, died tragically in the early hours of the very day his magnum opus was due to open in New York, 30 years ago.
It’s nonetheless a great deep dive into what made the young Larson tick, for diehard fans or as an introduction to his work, but these songs deserve a bit of narrative structure.
So, perhaps, it’s wise to present them as individual songs even if it makes for an uneven evening.
The Jonathan Larson Project is a must for fans of his work – both fascinating and slightly melancholy.

Anyone who loves musical theatre should make this show a priority. It is not merely a tribute to Jonathan Larson. It is compelling evidence that one of musical theatre's greatest talents left behind far more masterpieces than the world ever realised.
We absolutely love this show and will undoubtedly return.
It is a thrilling, bittersweet look at a genius finding his voice.

Performed by an outstanding cast of West End stars, The Jonathan Larson Project at The Southwark Playhouse Borough is an exciting evening of rediscovery that celebrates the legacy of an artist who has inspired, challenged and moved audiences around the world.
For fans of Jonathan Larson, this is a rare opportunity to discover another side of his extraordinary talent.
The Jonathan Larson Project is a song cycle conceived by Jennifer Ashley Tepper, consisting of songs taken from the revolutionary composer’s archives, tapes, and journals.
It is a company where every performer feels like a leading player, resulting in a consistently thrilling evening of musical theatre.
There are songs here I would love to hear again, and understanding how Larson progressed as an artist was enjoyable and instructive.
The Jonathan Larson Project helps to illustrate how there could have been so much more.
It may be imperfect and have a couple of issues it needs to address, but for the most part that actually adds to its charm.
The premise promises a fascinating exploration of one of musical theatre's most influential writers, but the production never quite fulfils that potential.

cn.t: Critics find this collection of Larson's rare and unheard songs a fascinating glimpse into a revolutionary talent, though some wish for more context. The performances impress, but the revue format divides opinion on whether it fully captures his genius.
